sentences.text: This appeal is preferred by the claimants challenging the judgment and award dated 30.01.2020 passed in MVC.No.655/2018 by II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hassan (for short 'the Tribunal').

entities.text: II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Hassan
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
Hence, the appellants seek enhancement of compensation.
Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are as under:
On 04.12.2017 at about 10.00 p.m., the deceased Krishnamurthy was proceeding on a motor cycle belonging to respondent No.1 bearing registration No.KA-13-E-9359 and when he reached Arkalgud Road, near Neralahalli circle to Haralikatte, another Usha vs Anand K M on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/138288248/
2 motor cycle bearing registration No.KA-13-EJ-6297 came in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety and collided with the vehicle ridden by deceased Krishnamurthy, which lead to the occurrence of accident.

Due to the said impact, the said Krishnamurthy sustained grievous injuries and was shifted to Arkalgud Government Hospital and further to Mani Hospital, Hassan and thereafter,
despite treatment, he succumbed to the injuries.
3.1 It is stated that the claimants spent more than Rs.2,00,000/- towards transportation, medical expenses NC: 2024:KHC:1695 and other obsequies ceremonies.
Hence, the claimants filed a claim petition seeking compensation.

3.2 On service of notice, respondents appeared through their counsel and filed their respective statement of objections denying the averments made in the claim petition including age, avocation, income, involvement of the vehicle and negligence attributed against the rider of the motor cycle.
Hence, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.
3.3 On the basis of pleadings, the tribunal framed the relevant issues for consideration.
3.4 In order to substantiate the issues and to establish the case, the claimants got examined witnesses as PWs.1 and 2 and got marked documents as Exs.P1 to P10.
On the other hand, respondents have neither led any evidence nor got marked any documents.

3.5 On the basis of material evidence, both oral and documentary and on hearing the submissions of learned NC: 2024:KHC:1695 counsels for both parties, the tribunal awarded compensation of Rs.16,82,800/- with interest @ 8% p.a. and directed respondent No.2-Insurance Company to pay the compensation.
3.6 Being aggrieved by the meager compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimants are before this Court challenging the impugned judgment and award.

4. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for appellants-claimants that the tribunal has erred in awarding meager compensation and has not taken into consideration the proper income for computation.
On these grounds, he seeks to enhance the compensation.
5. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company contends that there is no error in the impugned judgment and award passed by the tribunal and the same does not call for interference.
The tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation by adopting NC: 2024:KHC:1695 the correct income and multiplier.
On these grounds, he seeks to dismiss the appeal.

3 6.

Having heard the learned counsel for the appellant-claimant and learned counsel for respondent- Insurance Company and perused the impugned judgment and award, it is not in dispute that the accident occurred on 04.12.2017 at 10.00 p.m. involving two vehicles, in which one of the vehicles was ridden by the deceased Krishnamurthy and due to the collusion in the accident, he succumbed to the injuries.

To establish the same, the claimants have adduced evidence and produced documents as Exs.P1 to P10, the Police records, which would clearly indicate the involvement of the vehicle and FIR and chargesheet are laid against the rider of the offending vehicle and the same has not been challenged.
The medical records would got to show that the deceased having met with the accident, succumbed to the injuries.
Due to the occurrence of accident, the negligence is rightly attributed against the rider of the offending vehicle.
Now coming to the age, avocation and income as on the date of occurrence of accident, the tribunal assessed the income at Rs.9,000/-.

It applied the multiplier as '16', as the deceased was aged 32 years as on the date of occurrence of accident, so also, added 40% towards future prospects and deducted 1/3rd towards personal and living expenses, as there are three dependents, which do not call for interference and the same are retained.
The Legal Services Authority chart stipulates the notional income of Rs.11,000/- for the accident of the year 2017 as against Rs.9,000/- taken by the tribunal.

Therefore, the claimant would be entitled to the compensation of Rs.19,71,264/-
(Rs.11,000/- + 40% = Rs.15,400/- - 1/3rd = Rs.10,267/- x 12 x 16) towards loss of dependency as against Rs.16,12,800/- awarded by the tribunal.
8. The tribunal awarded Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium, which requires interference.

As per the decision of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of NC: 2024:KHC:1695 National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and others reported in (2017) 16 Supreme Court Cases 680, Rs.40,000/- to be awarded to each dependents towards loss of consortium along with 10%
escalation for one block period on the same.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In the present case, there are three dependants.

Therefore, this Court deems it appropriate to award Rs.1,20,000/- (Rs.40,000/- x 3) along with 10%
escalation, which would come to Rs.12,000/- (Rs.1,20,000/- x 10%).
In all, the claimants would be entitled to Rs.1,32,000/- towards loss of consortium.
9. The tribunal awarded Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate and Rs.15,000/- towards transportation of dead body, funeral expenses and obsequies ceremonies.
In all, Rs.30,000/- awarded by the tribunal towards conventional heads, which does not call for interference and the same is retained.

As per the aforesaid decision, 10% escalation for one block period on the same to be awarded under this head, which would come to Rs.33,000/- (Rs.30,000/- + 10%).
NC: 2024:KHC:1695 10.
In view of the above, the claimant would be entitled to a total compensation of Rs.21,36,264/- as against Rs.16,82,800/- as mentioned in the table below:
